Docs.summary:
The actions that define the template's orchestration. These are the same model a scenario publishes, and carry unresolved `%%\{...\}%%` macros; the macros are substituted when the scenario runs, not when it is read or created. Three macro namespaces may appear:
`%%\{parameters.\<name\>\}%%` — resolves from the parameter values supplied when the scenario is configured. The accepted names are declared by `parameters`.
`%%\{resourceTargeting.include.\<dimension\>\}%%` — resolves from the resource targeting of the scenario's configuration (for example `zones`, `locations`). The template does not declare these; they are dimensions of the configuration supplied at run time.
`%%\{filters.\<dimension\>\}%%` — deprecated spelling of `resourceTargeting.include.`, retained only so that superseded template versions keep resolving. Do not depend on it; the newest version of every template uses `resourceTargeting.include.`. An action's `failureBehavior` overrides the template-wide `failureBehavior` for that action alone; an action that does not carry one inherits the template-wide value.

Docs.summary: Template-wide default for how a scenario run reacts when one of this template's actions fails. An action that does not carry its own `failureBehavior` inherits this value; when neither is present the effective behavior is `Stop`. A scenario created from this template takes this policy with the rest of the template's structure, so it is also the scenario's resolved `failureBehavior`. Template versions published before this policy existed do not carry one and report it as absent, which the run resolves as `Stop`.
